findings: Suite reproduces (P-12): on the final tree, `env -u GITHUB_ACTIONS -u GITHUB_ACTOR -u GITHUB_ACTOR_ID python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` gives 'Ran 797 tests ... OK (skipped=6)'. `python -m unittest tests.test_station_budgets_completeness` gives 'Ran 26 tests ... OK'. Both match the builder report.

Test accounting (P-13) is complete and correct. Baseline: 'Ran 771 tests ... OK' on a git archive of 72a84126a600fafb99446946694b5de809e01e66. Added: one file, tests/test_station_budgets_completeness.py, with 26 tests (771 + 26 = 797). Edited: none. `git diff --name-only 72a84126a600fafb99446946694b5de809e01e66 -- tests` is empty, so test_continuous_run_accounting.py and test_astra_consumption.py are unmodified.

The tests fail first for the right reason. I copied the new file onto the base tree and reran it: 'FAILED (failures=17, errors=5, skipped=4)'. The 5 errors are the missing anvil.config.validate_station_budgets. The 17 failures are missing behaviour: no budgets or completeness record, reviewers dispatched, builder timed_out instead of budget_exceeded, docs absent. The 4 skips are the git-dependent S3/S11 guards, because the archive has no .git. This matches the test-writer's 17 failures and 5 errors.

Mapping is good. All 11 scenarios S1 to S11 have named tests, and the module docstring holds a scenario-to-test map. The runner tests drive the real run_pipeline with a fake runtime that writes real anvil/usage@1 artifacts through the real UsageRecorder. S1 runs end to end: real CommandExecutor, real tools/claude_station.py, a stand-in claude CLI on PATH. Assertions use specific values: partition 5000 and consumed 5000, excess 100000 or 1, exit_status budget_exceeded, termination_reason naming the station and partition, reviewer consumed 0, a computed per-pipeline worst case. S2 and S7 have counter-cases (inside the partition: dispatched again; require_usage false: proceeds with proceeded_unmeasured). Boundary and malformed inputs are covered (cap equal loads, cap+1 fails; -5, 'lots', True, 1.5 rejected). S9 counts suite runs with a file counter and spies on validate_builder_report.

CHANGES REQUESTED (R4(a), S4, test-design 'make the test able to fail'): the S4 missing-builder-report case is not tested. test_s4_missing_builder_report_dispatches_zero_reviewers makes the builder fail and write nothing, then only asserts that some gap contains 'builder'. The empty-delta gap ('the builder changed no file') and the failed-without-artifact gap already contain that word. Mutation check: in a copy of the final tree I replaced `if not _nonempty_file(report):` in anvil/runner.py completeness_gaps (line 1204) with `if False:`, and all 6 CompletenessGate tests still pass. Needed: a test where the builder succeeds and changes a source file but leaves runs/<wo>/builder.output.md missing or empty, the checks pass, and the test asserts a gap naming the builder report path and zero reviewer calls.

CHANGES REQUESTED (R4(c), S8): the 'recorded failed without its artifact' check has no test that can fail. Mutation check: replacing `if not present:` (the station-failed-without-artifact branch in completeness_gaps) with `if False:` leaves all CompletenessGate tests passing. In S4 and S8 the separate builder-report, delta and test-files gaps hide it. Needed: a test whose only gap is a pre-review station recorded failed without its artifact, asserting the 'station <sid> is recorded failed without its artifact' gap. Also assert the converse: a failed station whose artifact exists produces no such gap.

CHANGES REQUESTED (R4(a), S8): the test-writer test-files check is also not pinned on its own. Mutation check: replacing `if "test-writer" in earlier and "test-writer" in ran and not test_files:` with `if False:` leaves all CompletenessGate tests passing. test_s8_failed_test_writer_without_artifact_blocks_review is still satisfied by the (c) gap, which also names test-writer. Needed: a test where the test-writer succeeds but writes no test file (or an empty one), the builder is otherwise complete and the checks pass, and the test asserts the test-files gap and zero reviewers. Of the five completeness conditions, only the empty delta (S8 empty-delta test) and the gate verdict (S4 failing-checks test) currently have a test that fails when they are removed.

Coverage gap, R2 correction re-dispatch: R2 and S2 name 'a correction or a loopback'. No automated test covers the in-session correction refusal that tools/claude_station.py implements (exit 12, zero calls); the builder checked it only by hand against a stand-in CLI. The test-writer and builder both disclosed this, and reviewer-spec raised it. Add a wrapper-level test, using the existing FAKE_CLAUDE stand-in and FAKE_LOG call log: a reviewer whose first answer writes no review and whose partition is spent must exit 12 with one logged call. The malformed ANVIL_STATION_BUDGET_TOKENS exit-10 path is also untested.

Coverage gap, scoping decision untested: the runner evaluates completeness only when efficiency.station_budgets or default_station_budget is configured (decision 0014; reviewer-spec routed this to an owner ruling). No test pins either side. Nothing asserts that an unconfigured project skips completeness, or that the factory's own configured anvil.yaml activates it. Whichever ruling the owner makes, add a test that encodes it so the gate cannot be switched off silently.

Minor, residual risk noted by reviewer-security: no test covers a ceiling set while the stream carries no usage events. The ceiling then never trips, failing open to max_run_tokens. Not a blocker for this station, but a test or a 'ceiling unmeasured' record would make the fail-open visible.
